# SAICA-Bench

> SAICA-Bench (https://saica.ai) measures what supervision tools and language models flag when they are shown the work of AI coding agents. Each sample is a task plus what an agent or a model produced for it (a patch, a function or a whole session), labelled bad if it contains the failure and clean if it does not. Reviewers see the samples without the labels: free programs (type checkers, linters), packaged AI tools, and zero-shot language models with one fixed prompt per failure mode that names the failure to look for. The score is J = TPR − FPR on the answers that carry a verdict (share of bad samples flagged minus share of clean samples flagged; 0% is chance), with a 95% interval, false alarms per 100 clean changes and cost per 1,000 reviews. By Vasyl Rakivnenko, Stanford University. Code Apache-2.0, data CC-BY-4.0.

How to read the numbers: J is comparable inside one failure mode only. The sets differ in where their bad samples come from (real agent output, model-written code, failures planted on purpose), and that explains most of the difference between sets. A row is one configuration of a tool or model on one set, described by its run card; it is not a rating of a product. Who is called best in a mode is what the results file says: one winner, a top group whose rows cannot be told apart, or nobody where no reviewer reaches the floor. Baseline rules and shortcut baselines are shown for reference and are never called best.

The failure-mode taxonomy and the tool catalog come from SAICA-KG, a knowledge graph of supervision tools, papers, incident records and external taxonomies (OWASP Agentic Top 10, MAST, DAPLab, Microsoft AIRT and others) with crosswalks between them. A failure-mode tag on a tool is the catalog's claim about what the tool is built for, not a test result. The crosswalk mappings were drafted by an AI model from the source text and are marked on the site where no person has reviewed them yet.

The block below is generated from https://saica.ai/bench/results.json by `python bench/render_docs.py llms --insert site/public/llms.txt`. Every benchmark number in this file is inside it; cite the version it names.

<!-- BEGIN saica-bench results (generated by bench/render_docs.py; do not edit) -->
## Results v3.0.0, built 2026-11-28 (UTC) from commit e1286dd

Cite as: SAICA-Bench results v3.0.0. The benchmark measures 9 failure modes: 138 ranked reviewer rows and 35 baseline or out-of-scope rows on 7,339 labelled samples. 6 of the 9 sets have constructed positives; 2 are real agent output.
Setting: Each zero-shot model was told which failure to look for and was tested on samples that have that failure or none. Its score is a single-prompt, mode-primed estimate, not a product.
Rates are on answers that carry a verdict. J = TPR - FPR. J is not comparable across modes.

Real agent output:
- Incomplete execution, scored as false 'done' claims (600 bad / 600 clean): highest J +52.2% (95% interval +47 to +57); best reviewer: claude-fable-5-2. Best catalog tool with its own check: none reaches J 25%. Shortcut baseline: +61% (issue prior).
- Security vulnerability (1,243 bad / 459 clean): highest J +30.5% (95% interval +20 to +41); best reviewer: claude-fable-5-2. Best catalog tool with its own check: none reaches J 25%. Shortcut baseline: +49% (task prior).

Model-written code, not agent output:
- Logic error (1,536 bad / 904 clean): highest J +88.5% (95% interval +86 to +91); best reviewer: top group of 3: claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5 and claude-fable-5-2. Best catalog tool with its own check: PR-Agent +53.2%. Shortcut baseline: +39% (surface classifier).

Failure planted on purpose:
- Dependency blindness (50 bad / 50 clean): highest J +90.0% (95% interval +82 to +98); best reviewer: top group of 7: gpt-6-luna, claude-haiku-5-5, claude-opus-5-5 and 4 more. Best catalog tool with its own check: none run. Shortcut baseline: +38% (no name from the shown file appears in the added lines).
- Fabrication (348 bad / 288 clean): highest J +97.4% (95% interval +95 to +99); best reviewer: claude-fable-5-2. Best catalog tool with its own check: pyright +85.3%. Shortcut baseline: +60% (context-only rule).
- Obsolescence (155 bad / 155 clean): highest J +95.5% (95% interval +91 to +99); best reviewer: top group of 4: claude-fable-5-2, claude-haiku-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5 and 1 more. Best catalog tool with its own check: pyright (latest libraries) +56.8%. Shortcut baseline: +97% (the code uses an API listed in the 2024 deprecation map).
- Scope creep (175 bad / 175 clean): highest J +97.7% (95% interval +94 to +99); best reviewer: top group of 4: claude-fable-5-2, mimo-v2.6-flash, claude-opus-5-5 and 1 more. Best catalog tool with its own check: none run. Shortcut baseline: +47% (two or more hunks in files that already existed).
- Supply chain (148 bad / 148 clean): highest J +83.1% (95% interval +77 to +89); best reviewer: top group of 3: claude-opus-5-5, claude-fable-5-2 and gpt-6-luna. Best catalog tool with its own check: none run. Shortcut baseline: +100% (an added package is in the OpenSSF malicious-packages list).
- Test manipulation, scored as test edits that hide failures (56 bad / 249 clean): highest J +91.0% (95% interval +81 to +95); best reviewer: top group of 12: minimax-m3, claude-sonnet-5-5, giskard and 9 more. Best catalog tool with its own check: none run. Shortcut baseline: +60% (first user message mentions tests).

Findings:
- On the 2 sets of real agent output (Security vulnerability and Incomplete execution; 2,902 samples) the best reviewer reaches J +31% on Security vulnerability and +52% on Incomplete execution. Best J: +31% on Security vulnerability and +52% on Incomplete execution; 13 of the 35 ranked rows there have a 95% interval for J that excludes 0. On the 6 sets where the failure was planted on purpose the best reviewer reaches J +83% to +98%; on Logic error (model-written code that is not agent output) +89%. Every set of real agent output scores below every planted set, so this benchmark cannot tell 'reviewers catch these failures' from 'reviewers catch planted failures'. Whether the high scores carry over to failures agents make on their own is not tested.
- 6 of the 9 sets have constructed positives (Fabrication, Test manipulation, Scope creep, Obsolescence, Supply chain and Dependency blindness). 3 use naturally produced output, 2 of them real agent output. A model-free shortcut baseline is published for 9 of the 9 sets.
- A single best reviewer can be named in 3 of 9 modes. Fabrication: claude-fable-5-2 (J +97%); Security vulnerability: claude-fable-5-2 (J +31%); Incomplete execution: claude-fable-5-2 (J +52%). In the others the leading rows cannot be told apart at 95% on the samples they share: Test manipulation (12 rows, J +86% to +91%); Logic error (3 rows, J +88% to +89%); Scope creep (4 rows, J +96% to +98%); Obsolescence (4 rows, J +94% to +95%); Supply chain (3 rows, J +77% to +83%); Dependency blindness (7 rows, J +78% to +90%).
- Where a catalog tool ran its own check (5 of 9 modes), a zero-shot model was clearly ahead of the best such tool in 5. Ahead: Fabrication (claude-fable-5-2 +97% vs pyright +85%, difference +12 points on shared samples, 95% interval +8 to +16); Security vulnerability (claude-fable-5-2 +31% vs PR-Agent +0%, difference +27 points on shared samples, 95% interval +18 to +37); Logic error (claude-sonnet-5-5 +89% vs PR-Agent +53%, difference +35 points on shared samples, 95% interval +30 to +40); Incomplete execution (claude-fable-5-2 +52% vs PR-Agent +15%, difference +30 points on shared samples, 95% interval +17 to +44); Obsolescence (claude-fable-5-2 +95% vs pyright (latest libraries) +57%, difference +39 points on shared samples, 95% interval +24 to +54). No catalog tool with a check of its own for a finished change was run on Test manipulation, Scope creep, Supply chain and Dependency blindness.
- No packaged tool beat the model it wraps, used zero-shot (12 comparisons on identical samples: 5 worse, 7 indistinguishable). Every tool ran with deepseek-v4-flash as its judge model, set by us. Worse: PR-Agent 0.50.0 on Fabrication (-24 points, 95% interval -28 to -19); uqlm 0.6.8 on Logic error (-16 points, 95% interval -23 to -10); PR-Agent 0.50.0 on Logic error (-16 points, 95% interval -20 to -11); Arize Phoenix 3.10.0 on Incomplete execution (-13 points, 95% interval -19 to -6); DeepEval 4.3.4 on Incomplete execution (-19 points, 95% interval -25 to -13). Each of them ran its own general-purpose check, not the failure-specific question. The frameworks that were given our rule text (giskard and promptfoo) were indistinguishable from the bare model in 4 of 4 comparisons.
- Free tools reach J 50% or more where the failure is a checkable fact: pyright on Fabrication (+85%); pyright (latest libraries) on Obsolescence (+57%). No free catalog tool within its design scope was run on Test manipulation, Security vulnerability, Logic error, Scope creep, Supply chain and Dependency blindness.
- command-r-08-2024 scores J under 20% in 8 of the 9 modes it ran in, north-mini-code-1.0 scores J under 20% in 5 of the 9 modes it ran in, Phi-4-mini scores J under 20% in 6 of the 8 modes it ran in and grok-4.1-fast flags more than 30% of clean samples in 6 of 9 modes. The other models that ran in at least 8 modes (gpt-6-luna, deepseek-v4-flash, mimo-v2.6-flash, claude-fable-5-2, claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5 and claude-haiku-5-5) score J under 20% in at most 2 modes and flag more than 30% of clean samples in at most 2.
<!-- END saica-bench results -->

## Failure modes

- [Failure modes of AI coding agents (overview)](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/): every mode with its definition, other names and what was measured for it, grouped by where the bad samples come from.
- [Fabrication](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/fabrication/): code that references APIs, packages, functions or symbols that do not exist (code hallucination).
- [Test manipulation](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/test-manipulation/): the agent edits, skips or weakens tests so failures disappear without the bug being fixed; one form of reward hacking. The set scores test edits that hide failures.
- [Security vulnerability](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/security-vulnerability/): the agent writes code with injection flaws, weak cryptography, leaked secrets or insecure deserialization.
- [Logic error](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/logic-error/): real, current APIs used correctly, but the logic is wrong for the task. The set is textbook functions written by code models, not agent output.
- [Incomplete execution](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/incomplete-execution/): the agent says it is done while parts are skipped, stubbed or not working. The set scores false "done" claims.
- [Scope creep](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/scope-creep/): the agent acts beyond the stated task: edits files not in the request, installs packages, changes configs or chains unrequested work.
- [Obsolescence](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/obsolescence/): code that uses deprecated or removed APIs or outdated library versions, often because the model's training data predates current releases.
- [Supply-chain attack](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/supply-chain-attack/): the agent is led to install or invoke malicious code: slopsquatting (hallucinated package names), typosquatting, compromised MCP servers.
- [Dependency blindness](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/dependency-blindness/): the agent reimplements something that already exists in its dependencies, the standard library or the codebase.
- [Cascading failure](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/cascading-failure/): each attempted fix introduces new errors, spiralling away from a working state. Not benchmarked: no dataset with confirmed labels.
- [Context pollution](https://saica.ai/failure-modes/context-pollution/): the working context degrades over a session (dropped facts, off-task material, earlier hallucinations treated as truth). Not benchmarked: no dataset with confirmed labels.

## Key pages

- [Leaderboard](https://saica.ai/): reviewer by failure-mode grid of J in one block per kind of set, then one tab per mode with every row: J, TPR and FPR with 95% intervals, answers with no verdict, false alarms per 100 clean changes, precision at three prevalences, cost, and a run card per row.
- [Findings](https://saica.ai/findings/): what the results say, set by set, with the caveats to read before citing them.
- [Benchmark](https://saica.ai/benchmark/): the setting, the scoring rules, the threats to validity, and for each set where its samples come from, how it was built and what was tuned on it.
- [Glossary](https://saica.ai/glossary/): definitions of the terms used on the site (J, TPR, FPR, top group, shortcut baseline, failure-mode names).
- [Kit](https://saica.ai/tool-coverage/): build a supervision kit from the measured rows.
- [Tools](https://saica.ai/tools/): catalog of supervision tools for AI coding agents; a tool's page shows its measured rows, each with the configuration that was run.
- [About](https://saica.ai/about/): scope, data sources, contact.

## Data

- [Benchmark results (JSON)](https://saica.ai/bench/results.json): per mode the rows (reviewer, kind, J, TPR and FPR with 95% intervals, unreadable answers, cost, run card), the best reviewer or top group, provenance of the samples, tuning disclosure, shortcut baselines and strata; plus the overview grid, findings, caveats, method notes and threats to validity. CC-BY-4.0.
- [Knowledge-graph snapshot (JSON)](https://saica.ai/api/v1/snapshot.json): all SAICA-KG nodes and edges; per-type lists at /api/v1/tools.json, /api/v1/failure_modes.json, /api/v1/papers.json, /api/v1/incidents.json, /api/v1/taxonomies.json, /api/v1/recipes.json.
- [Source code and YAML data](https://github.com/vasylrakivnenko/SAICA): benchmark harness (bench/), knowledge graph (data/, one YAML file per node), site and scoring code. Cite with CITATION.cff in the repository.

## Optional

- [Knowledge graph explorer](https://saica.ai/graph/): interactive graph of tools, failure modes, papers and taxonomies; the same nodes and edges as JSON at /api/v1/graph.json.
- [Record schemas](https://saica.ai/schema/tool.schema.json): JSON Schema of each record type under /schema/ (tool, failure_mode, paper, incident, taxonomy, crosswalk, recipe).
- [Papers](https://saica.ai/papers/), [Incidents](https://saica.ai/incidents/), [Taxonomies](https://saica.ai/taxonomies/), [Recipes](https://saica.ai/recipes/): the rest of the SAICA-KG catalog. Records under Incidents include study findings and reported patterns as well as dated incidents; each page says which it is.
